title: How electronic paper (electronic ink) displays imitate ink on paper

sources.title: Books of the Future: the Engineering Behind Electronic Ink Displays
Driving Waveform Design of Electrophoretic Display Based on Optimized Particle Activation for a Rapid Response Speed
sources.note: 只取事實（重新整理畫面時把整個畫面驅動成全黑、全白以消除殘影）

facts.text: Electronic paper is a reflective display: like a printed page, it shows images with the light around it and has no backlight.
Electronic ink is made of tiny capsules filled with a clear liquid in which white and black particles float.
The white particles carry a positive charge and the black ones a negative charge; a voltage pulls one color to the visible surface.
The particles stay where they were last moved, so a page stays on screen without power; energy is used only to change the image.
Many e-readers can run for weeks on a single charge.
Electronic ink screens respond and refresh more slowly than LCD screens, so they are poor at video.
Color electronic paper exists but has been limited; most devices show black, white and gray.
Because they reflect surrounding light, e-paper screens are easy to read in well-lit places.
To clear faint traces of earlier images, e-paper is driven fully to black and white, which appears as a brief flash.
